topicName: Cluster Autoscaling, HPA, VPA, and KEDA
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Autoscaling in Kubernetes: Cluster Autoscaler, HPA, VPA, and KEDA"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kubernetes autoscaling is essential for maintaining application performance while optimizing cloud infrastructure costs. In this tutorial, we will explore the four primary pillars of Kubernetes scaling: Cluster Autoscaler, Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA), Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA), and Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling (KEDA)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"HPA automatically scales the number of pods in a deployment, replication controller, or replica set based on observed CPU utilization or other custom metrics. It targets the application layer by adding or removing pod replicas."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: php-apache-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: php-apache
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 50"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA)"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"While HPA scales out (adding more pods), VPA scales up (allocating more CPU and memory to existing pods). VPA recommends or automatically updates resource requests and limits for your containers based on historical usage."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: "autoscaling.k8s.io/v1"
kind: VerticalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: php-apache-vpa
spec:
  targetRef:
    apiVersion: "apps/v1"
    kind: "Deployment"
    name: "php-apache"
  updatePolicy:
    updateMode: "Auto""},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Cluster Autoscaler"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Cluster Autoscaler operates at the infrastructure level. It adjusts the size of your Kubernetes cluster when pods fail to launch due to insufficient resources, or when nodes are underutilized and their pods can be scheduled onto other nodes."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scale-Up Trigger: Triggered when pending pods exist due to insufficient CPU or memory capacity on current nodes."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scale-Down Trigger: Triggered when node utilization drops below a configurable threshold (default 50%) for an extended period."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling (KEDA)"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"KEDA is a single-purpose and lightweight component that allows you to application-scale your workloads based on events from external sources like Azure Service Bus, AWS SQS, Apache Kafka, or Prometheus metrics. KEDA can even scale workloads down to zero."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: aws-sqs-scaledobject
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: worker-app
  minReplicaCount: 0
  maxReplicaCount: 10
  triggers:
  - type: aws-sqs-queue
    metadata:
      queueURL: https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123456789012/my-queue
      queueLength: "5""},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Combining Autoscalers"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Avoid running HPA and VPA concurrently on the same resource metrics (like CPU/Memory) to prevent conflicting scaling loops."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use HPA or KEDA for handling traffic bursts, and pair them with Cluster Autoscaler to ensure underlying nodes scale gracefully."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always set appropriate resource requests and limits before implementing VPA or HPA."}]
